quote: So I think that with those trees still there, I don't think that the panels will be able to get enough sun
stewart_read: Rep disqualifies on a visual/Google Maps guess without asking follow-up questions about which side of the roof, tree height, or seasonal shade — a premature, under-informed DQ.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be trained to move fast to protect their own time on low-fit leads, but the customer's own later correction shows the DQ was made too early.
coaching_implication: Ask 2-3 clarifying questions (which roof face, how much of the day, tree height/trim plans) before disqualifying — the visual read from a map is not sufficient evidence.

quote: Once I once I have that side gets a lot.
stewart_read: Customer is actively trying to keep the opportunity alive with a specific correction, and the rep lets the line pass without acknowledgment or follow-up question.
coaching_implication: When a customer volunteers a qualifying detail after a DQ, the rep should pause and ask a direct follow-up ('which side gets the most sun, and for how long?') instead of letting it pass.

quote: only only give shade on the portion of the house and only a part of the day, if that makes a difference.
stewart_read: This is the second time the customer offers evidence contradicting the DQ, and the rep again does not investigate, instead reiterating the space concern.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to re-open qualification rather than restate the DQ — a 'let me note that down for the design team' response at minimum keeps the door open honestly.

quote: It's a ton of space to put panels up there, unfortunately.
stewart_read: Customer's pushback functions like an objection to the DQ itself; rep restates the original concern rather than reframing or investigating, effectively conceding the conversation is over.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is stronger — there's no evidence the rep is setting up a deliberate later move; the vague callback promise that follows reads as an exit line, not a strategic hold.
coaching_implication: Instead of restating the space concern, rep could say 'that's helpful — let me flag that for the design team specifically, since partial shade changes things' to genuinely leave the door open.

quote: I can reach out to my design team and see if they would be able to do anything. And then if they can, I'll give you a callback, and we could totally get you scheduled. Okay?
stewart_read: No specific day/time is offered, no ownership of a concrete next step is stated — this is a vague promise, not a booked callback.
coaching_implication: If the rep intends to escalate to design team, they should state a specific timeframe ('I'll call you back by Thursday') rather than leaving it open-ended.

quote: I really do apologize, but I can get you off our list if you don't get any more calls. Okay?
stewart_read: Rep offers to remove customer from the list before the customer has even finished clarifying the shading situation, effectively closing the door prematurely.
coaching_implication: Hold off on offering list removal until qualification questions are fully explored — this line preempted the customer's own correction.
